title: Quantization recipe envelopes & delta-apply protocol for reproducible calibration artifacts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a canonical, signed "recipe envelope" format and a compact delta-apply protocol so calibration and quant artifacts are reproducible, traceable, and efficiently versioned. The envelope should capture everything required to deterministically re-run calibration and produce the same quant artifact (or a byte-identical derivative when applying a delta), and should be stored in the artifact registry with content-addressable identifiers and signed provenance metadata.
background: We currently emit quantized model files and ad-hoc metadata blobs. Reproducing a quant artifact requires manual coordination (tooling versions, seed, dataset slice, kernel selection). This causes operational friction for rollbacks, audits, and customer reproducibility requests. Existing tickets cover checksums and rollbacks; this task is focused on a declarative envelope + delta protocol to make small profile changes cheap and traceable.
acceptance_criteria: Define a canonical envelope JSON schema (human-readable) that includes: model checkpoint digest, training/float-checkpoint reference, calibration dataset snapshot id, calibration seed, deterministic RNG details, toolchain version, quant hyperparameters (per-layer and global), kernel/runtime hints, and an optional signed operator note.
Implement canonicalization and canonical-hash compute (JCS-like) so identical envelopes always produce identical digests despite key ordering differences.
Add deterministic signing mechanism (ECDSA P-256) for envelopes stored in the registry; store signer id and signature as top-level envelope fields.

Create a binary delta-apply format for profile changes that is content-aware (per-layer diffs) and can be applied to a base quant artifact to produce a new artifact with a computed digest; deltas are small and addressable via content hashes.
End-to-end CI: given a commit with envelope + calibration seed, CI reproduces the quant artifact and validates the artifact digest matches the one published by the calibration job.
APIs/CLI for: publish-envelope, fetch-envelope, apply-delta, replay-calibration; all commands accept explicit registry digest and verify signatures.

Run a 10-model smoke suite showing replay fidelity: byte-identical artifact for 6/10 models when full replaying enforced, bit-stable deltas for the other 4 with acceptable accuracy delta (<0.5% top-1 change).
Documentation and a short runbook for rollback: how to find matching envelope, verify signature, apply delta, and re-deploy on Dedicated/Private clusters.
Security review sign-off for envelope signing and registry access controls.
plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): design envelope schema and canonicalization rules; implement hash and signing helpers. Phase 2 (week 3-4): prototype registry storage for envelopes and delta format; wire CLI for publish/fetch. Phase 3 (week 5): integrate CI reproducibility checks and run smoke suite; gather results and iterate. Phase 4 (post-merge): docs, runbook, and rollout to runtime canary.
tasks: Draft envelope schema and get PM/design sign-off
Implement canonical JSON serializer and hasher
Add signing library and test vectors
Design delta format and layer-aware diff algorithm
Implement publish/fetch CLI and registry endpoints
Add CI reproducibility job and goldenset checks
Security review and access policy adjustments
risks: Determinism assumptions: hardware-dependent kernels may introduce nondeterminism. We mitigate by including kernel selection hints and an experiment to mark 'deterministic-safe' kernels. Delta application complexity: per-layer diffs must be validated to avoid accuracy regressions; include safety checks and optional bloom filters for layer mismatch detection.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for canonicalization and hash vectors. 2) Integration test: reproduce calibration job on CI with frozen dataset snapshot and seed. 3) Delta-apply test: apply delta to base artifact and verify digest and model outputs on a small eval set. 4) Regression test: run the 10-model smoke suite under canary runtime.
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag; enable for internal calibration jobs first. Run reproducibility CI on every calibration commit for 2 weeks. If stable, flip flag for external quant build pipeline and then promote to dedicated runtime canary. Maintain ability to roll back to previously signed envelope/registered digest via CLI helper.
notes: Security asked for signer rotation plan and HSM compatibility — follow-up item created. PM asked that artifact registry entries link to customer-facing audit IDs when requested. Design requested a compact human-readable summary for each envelope for the console UI.
